panel.heading: Task
panel.dropFiles: Drop files to attach them to this task

attach.title: Files
attach.deleteFolderConfirm: Delete the folder {{name}} and everything in it?

help.title: taskmgr shortcuts
help.hint: press q, esc or enter to close

move.desc: move between tasks (or works and repositories on the tree)

nav.desc: move between Origins, task areas and Task details

toTree.keys: h from the leftmost task area
toTree.desc: over to the work / repository tree

treeRow.keys: a / i / e / o / d / space on the tree
treeRow.desc: add into the row (a work into an origin, a repository into a work), edit it, programming on a repository (its source code in VS Code), open its folder, delete it, preview it (its description and what else it has)

tab.desc: switch between the tree and the tasks

add.desc: add a task (a subtask of the selected task, when there is one)

unselect.desc: drop the selection, so a / n add a task at the top

code.desc: programming: open the repository of the selected task in VS Code, on this computer

into.desc: into the selected task (its subtasks) / up out of it

parent.desc: to the parent path: out of a task's subtasks, then repository → work → origin → all origins

copy.desc: copy the selected task's id for tm run (repository:id or work:id)

text.desc: in a text: cut the caret's line (nothing selected) / select all the text

preview.desc: open the task dialog: edit task.txt and its prompt, saved with Save (⌘S)

files.desc: select a file, open its preview

prompt.keys: j / k, enter on Task with the prompt shown
prompt.desc: move between the text, the prompt and the files; enter edits the one chosen

promptEdit.desc: show the task's prompt and move to it, hide it again (in the panel, or in the task dialog once esc left the text); enter or e edits it

run.keys: ⌘ / ctrl + enter in the prompt; r in the task dialog
run.desc: run the task's prompt with Claude Code

scheduler.desc: t shows the task in the right pane, s the scheduler (its text is edited as in vim: h j k l move, i / a type, esc goes back; on a task, space opens it, enter starts a new line under it, x / p / w mark it and backspace / d removes it)

calendar.desc: show the calendar, a whole month, in the middle in place of the tasks, with the scheduler at the right (t is back on the tasks; v goes through the list, the progress view and the calendar; on the calendar, h j k l choose a day at once (after esc, j goes back into the month), enter goes into the day, where j / k choose an event and space shows it, and n adds an event in Apple Calendar on the day chosen; esc goes back out)

timetable.desc: on the scheduler: show or hide the day's timetable under its page (the day's events in Google and Apple Calendar; after esc, j goes down to it: j / k walk its events, h / l step a day, space shows an event, n adds one in Apple Calendar)

switch.desc: switch between this computer's page and the server's (the link at the right end of the status bar)

machines.desc: open Machines Run (a prompt or a /command on the machines)

add.pathEmpty: Give a tasks folder or a source folder.

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.missing: This task is not on this machine
scheduler.calendarHelpIntro: A calendar is added by the address of its ICS feed: paste the address and save; whether it is a Google or an Apple one is told from the address. The name is optional (the calendar's own is used when it is left empty). Add a row for each calendar, of as many accounts as needed.
scheduler.calendarHelpGoogle: Google Calendar on the web > Settings > the calendar at the left > "Integrate calendar" > copy "Secret address in iCal format".
scheduler.calendarHelpApple: Calendar (on a Mac, an iPhone or iCloud.com) > the calendar > Share > turn on "Public Calendar" > copy its webcal:// link.
scheduler.calendarHelpSecret: An address is a secret: whoever has it can read the calendar. The list is kept in taskmgr.json and synced with it.

analysis.title: Income analysis
analysis.inYearNote: Counted from each monthly item's start month
analysis.onceNote: Undated, not in the annual figures

machines.prompt: What should Claude do on the machine?
machines.runHint: Run Claude Code with this prompt on the machines ticked (⌘ / ctrl + enter)
machines.none: No machine syncs with this server yet: start taskmgrd on one, with AI_RUNNER=1 in its .env.
machines.forgetConfirm: Remove {{name}} from the machines? The folders it synced are kept, as this server's own. It is back at its next sync.
machines.commandsOnly: /commands only: AI_RUNNER=1 in its .env runs Claude Code there
